Complex interactions between temperature setpoints at different locations in the system, variations in air flow rate, changing environmental conditions, and other factors affecting the loads make it challenging to understand what the relative impacts are from the HEDS-optimized controls and the energy recovery reheat coil. To differentiate the savings due to the HEDS HVAC optimization software from those due to reheat in the cooling recovery coil (CRC), we performed an analysis to estimate operation of the HEDS in CAV and VAV operating modes with the same optimized control settings but without the CRC energy recovery activated. This hypothetical operation corresponds to the hardware configuration used for the CAV and VAV baseline configurations but without the CRC coil, so comparisons between the “HEDS without CRC” modes and the baseline configurations provide an indication of the energy savings that result from the automated control strategies employed by the HEDS operation. With the same control settings, the zone conditions are assumed to remain the same as in the normal HEDS mode, so the Space_load, Fan_power and Misc_load values remain identical. With CRC operation deactivated, however, the chilled water load and VAV reheat coil energy would be increased to achieve the same operating conditions. Consequently, the chiller electrical power required would also increase proportionally to the chilled water load. This analysis allows us to estimate the portion of the load reductions that were achieved as a result of the HEDS-optimized control settings separately from those due to the CRC operation.
